21 Three springs are arranged vertically as shown.
P
Q
R
W
Springs P and Q are identical and each has spring constant k. Spring R has spring constant 3k.
What is the increase in the overall length of the arrangement when a force W is applied as
shown?
A
k
W
6
5
B
k
W
3
4
C
2
7 kW
D
4 kW

hints: Notice from the diagram that P and Q are side by side above the bar while R is below the bar, so the bar movement equals the P-Q extension and the bottom point moves further by the R extension.
Connect the forces to Hooke's law $F = kx$: R carries the full force $W$ but P and Q share $W$ equally so each carries $W/2$.
Calculate $x = F/k$ for R with stiffness $3k$ and for P with stiffness $k$ and force $W/2$, then add the two extensions for the overall increase in length.
walkthrough: Identify the combination: P and Q are in parallel above the bar, and that parallel pair is in series with R below the bar.
Use equilibrium for spring R: it supports the applied force, so $F_R = W$. With $F = kx$, its extension is $x_R = W/(3k)$.
Use equilibrium for the bar: P and Q together support $W$, so by symmetry each supports $W/2$. Their extension is the drop of the bar, $x_P = (W/2)/k = W/(2k)$.
Add the series extensions to get the movement of the $W$ point relative to the ceiling: $x = x_P + x_R = W/(2k) + W/(3k)$.
Combine with common denominator 6: $x = 3W/(6k) + 2W/(6k) = 5W/(6k)$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Sum of $W/(2k)$ from P and Q plus $W/(3k)$ from R gives $5W/(6k)$.

B.explanation: Too large because it overestimates the load on P and Q or the extension of R.

C.explanation: Wrong because $kW$ has units of $\text{N}^2\text{m}^{-1}$, not a length.

D.explanation: Wrong because $kW$ has units of $\text{N}^2\text{m}^{-1}$, not a length.
